minutes.headline: Schools urged town unity ahead of the override vote; routine grants and policy readings were approved
minutes.summary: The meeting was dominated by the superintendent and chair urging the town to approach the upcoming Proposition 2½ override and town meeting collaboratively rather than divisively, describing this year's tri-board budget process as unusually transparent. The committee also heard a LEAF Foundation fundraising update, approved two state grant submissions and a farm-to-school grant, discussed a scholarship trust/EIN dispute with the town's Trust Commission, revisited unified sports options, reviewed the quarterly budget and personnel reports, assigned negotiating teams for two union contracts, set a process for the superintendent's evaluation, and waived first readings on four policies.

budget_items.what_was_said: Two one-time scholarships were donated by the Artisans of Hickory Hills (care of Donna Silverstein) for graduating seniors pursuing collegiate visual arts studies.
One warrant was presented for committee signature this evening.
The business manager reported there were no line item transfers this cycle.
The LEAF Foundation president reported funds raised to date and described a matching challenge from a local resident that doubles donations through May 31.
A state grant proposal for locally procured produce, staff training, classroom curriculum and community outreach on healthy/affordable food.
A state grant for professional development, job-embedded coaching, PD days and stipends tied to implementing high-quality instructional materials.
A second-round state grant, this time for pre-K curriculum (likely Boston Public Schools open-source materials); the presenter asked for flexibility since a final dollar amount was not yet set.
A member noted the Prism grants are more needed because of a federal cut to Title I funding.
An example was given of a donor giving a lump sum to a trust-held scholarship that the district draws down over time.
The business manager reported year-to-date expenditure percentage, comparable to the same point last year.
A member questioned the balance and spending in the Chapter 658 (athletics) revolving fund and asked about sweeping small, inactive revolving funds like the vending machine fund.
A member asked how a reported overage on electricity (around 101% expended) would be absorbed; the business manager said funds could be moved within budget and he was not worried.
Members discussed absorbing what had been a surplus at the same point last year so it does not recur.
The extended day revolving fund is running close to break-even or slightly negative; members agreed to consider raising fees at a future meeting rather than risk closing the program.

budget_items.topic: State House budget / Chapter 70 and circuit breaker
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair noted the House budget released that day included additional per-pupil Chapter 70 money and some additional special education circuit breaker funding, with the exact amount still pending the cherry sheet.

decisions.decision: Business manager to look into whether inactive/old revolving funds with minimal balances can be swept or closed.
Agreed to place an extended day program fee increase on a future meeting agenda rather than let the program run unsustainably.
Business manager to find out where a departed paraprofessional went after resigning.
Negotiating team assignments set: Emily paired on cafeteria workers' contract talks, Laura and Mandy paired on custodians' contract talks.
Members to submit their superintendent evaluation rubric scores/comments by roughly May 13, ahead of compilation and discussion at the May 20 meeting.

what_happened.line: The superintendent and chair urged residents to approach the coming override vote and town meeting collaboratively, calling this year's budget process unusually transparent.
The committee voted to submit two Prism grant applications and a Farm to Table grant to bring in state funding for staff training and curriculum.
A dispute over a scholarship trust fund's EIN with the town's Trust Commission was sent to legal counsel rather than resolved tonight.
First readings were waived on four policies, including student data privacy and security rules that address AI use.
Negotiating teams were assigned for the custodians' and cafeteria workers' union contracts, and a fee increase for the extended day program was pushed to a future agenda.

why_it_matters: The override and town meeting the superintendent referenced would set the tax bill residents vote on, and the meeting framed this year's budget process as more transparent than past years.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.coverage: official minutes are a summary only
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the small set of hard facts the official minutes actually state — the warrant total, the Prism III grant amount, the $8,366 LEAF total, the $160/pupil House budget figure, and the four policy numbers being waived — but the official minutes are a thin summary that omits nearly all of the meeting's financial discussion (quarterly-report percentages, revolving-fund balances, the electricity overage, the extended-day fee rate, the prior-year surplus, the Title I cut, and every non-procedural decision except negotiating assignments), while our minutes, built from captions, could not resolve any vote's outcome. The one thing a reader should specifically check is the Prism II/III grant vote and the cafeteria-negotiations pairing, both of which read inconsistently between the two records.
